data.name: Depression Quest
data.detailed_description:
Depression Quest is an interactive fiction game where you play as someone living with depression. You are given a series of everyday life events and have to attempt to manage your illness, relationships, job, and possible treatment. This game aims to show other sufferers of depression that they are not alone in their feelings, and to illustrate to people who may not understand the illness the depths of what it can do to people.

  • Over 40k words of interactive fiction.
    Playthroughs are short enough to be done in one day, but long enough for the game to have gotten it's point across.
  • About 150 unique encounters.
    Based on your depression levels, different choices open and close off to you.
  • Content generated based on your decisions.
    The choices you make have a real effect on how your playthrough turns out.
  • Multiple endings.
    See how your choices affected the game's world, and how well you've managed your depression.
  • Audio and visuals react to your depression.
    Listen as the music gets glitchier and see how much stronger the static gets. Watch the color get sucked out of how you see the world.

reviews.review:
About as emotional as a wet napkin, about as functional as baby's first hello word program. This game was the start of a gigantic butterfly effect that has lead us to the current geopolitical situation because the creator(s) made a shallow game that can be completed in literally 5 minutes if you read a bit fast and were too egotistical to realize that shit like this is worth at most 10 minutes of screwing around on some random website you found while clicking random links on Tumblr (BECAUSE THIS IS A WEB GAME!).

My issues with this "game" is that just like recent releases that were astroturfed and then copulated with the press to ensure that they would give 10/10s like clapping seals, there is no game here. It wants to be "an RPG", but it was clearly made by someone who has never played RPGs. It is extremely hard to RolePlay as the MC in something as badly written.

You get very little meaningful choices and the ones for a good ending are obvious. This game is about as open as the Hormuz Straight and about as impactful as a Nerf gun. No matter what you choose the story unfolds in basically the same way, events are treated in the same fashion regardless of your state, which is so stupid because someone who is barely functional and is constantly having anxiety attacks cannot go out to attend dinners with their family and the other bull that this game's narrative pushes onto you.
The endings that i managed to get out of this were a good and a bad one, both sucked. In the good ending you feel a tad better about yourself and it hits you with "things are going better but you will never not be depressed" which is massive bs because depression CAN be overcome with a lot of work (which the devs clearly didn't want to put in representing lmao). In the bad ending i genuinely expected suicide of the MC but it just goes on with his awful life made worse by bad decisions.

The controls were somehow underwhelming for an electron web game but here we are. The choices are presented with a number in front of them so those with pattern recognition might expect the ability to press the corresponding number on their keyboard in order make their selection, however this game was made by someone LARPing as a game dev while actually having barely any knowledge of JavaScript, so the keyboard does F U C K ALL! A round of applause for the keyboard controls: tab to move selection down, shift+tab to move selection up, enter to select, backspace to go back. If you've ever used a web browser you'd know that this just what's already there for navigating web pages. They also broke gamepad support on the Linux version which is so funny considering that it's literally just a Chrome page. Impressive work for being one of the "games" that contributed to the death of Greenlight! I made better games in JS in 7 days with the budget of a bottle of Arizona Tea as someone who knew nothing about front-end web development, you have zero excuses!

Now there's also the music in this game which is... there, but it's mid and repetitive for a lack of better words so i turned it off in the OS audio panel becaues there's no way to turn it off in game.

This game tries to invoke some emotions by showing you a little pic of the current scene, most of these images however are quite generic and feel like something taken from shutterstock. They're supposed to gradually become filled with static as you get more depressed, but who the hell cares when the story is always the same?

Lastly there's the game's very topic at hand and its total failure to meaningfully represent the struggle with depression. Actions taken by the player are effortless and meaningless, the struggle is only ever narrated but isn't translated into an actual gameplay feature which is why i don't like this game. Depression at times feels like you're Atlas carrying your entire world on your back while everyone is spitting on you and your body is begging to let go, but clicking the next option in this game always feels the same, there's no real emotion to it. The writing is supposed to help it but it's genuinely Tumblr fanfic levels so the rest of the very shaky foundations of this "game" need to carry it, which they can't because there's nothing.

Overall i consider this "game" the first Mixtapelike, so it's a 0/10, as in my opinion this doesn't classify as a "game" but it classifies as a webpage with a state machine that's more linear than a tram train. Genuinely if the authors knew their place and just shut the hell up once in their life the world woud be a better place. But nooooo, Zoe just had to sleep with 5 dudes in the gaming industry, just so they could network and use that power to shut down critiques from above while cheating on their boyfriend. They just had to be an insufferable cunt and now everyone is worse off for it. Thank you Zoe, i hope it was worthwile, i hope the power feels good because playing Depression Quest sure wasn't.
